# Leslie Moore

## Overview

- **Age:** Twenty-eight  <sub>[v4 c10 P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c5 P8](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0008)</sub>
- **Status:** Remarried (formerly widowed)  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c38 P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds (West farm), Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c5 P0](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0000), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035)</sub>
- **Role:** Former schoolteacher and boarding-house keeper  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035)</sub>

## Appearance

Leslie is an exceptionally beautiful woman with sea-blue eyes and an abundance of living, burnished golden hair that reaches to her feet when uncoiled. She has a high-bred, splendid figure, an ivory-tinted skin, and a crimson mouth. She often wears a touch of red or crimson in her clothing to complement her looks.

_Sources: [v4 c5 P8](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0008), [v4 c10 P28](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0028), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P15](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0015), [v4 c21 P5](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0005), [v4 c23 P25](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0025)_

## Personality

Though originally warm, passionate, and vivid, years of tragedy and isolation made Leslie reserved, proud, and occasionally bitter. She harbors a fierce pride and an unyielding sense of duty, refusing to shirk any responsibility she has assumed. When freed from her tragic circumstances, her natural warmth, wit, and capacity for joy and deep love re-emerge.

_Sources: [v4 c10 P43](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0043), [v4 c11 P29](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0029), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011), [v4 c25 P15](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0015), [v4 c30 P29](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0029)_

## History

Leslie Moore lived a tragic early life in Four Winds, marked by the horrific accidental death of her brother Kenneth and the suicide of her father. At sixteen, she sacrificed her ambitions of attending college to marry Dick Moore in order to prevent her mother from being turned out of her mortgaged home. Shortly after her mother's death, Dick went to sea and was reported lost. Years later, Captain Jim found him in a Havana hospital suffering from brain-trauma amnesia and brought him back. For twelve years, Leslie nursed the helpless man, taking in summer boarders to support them. When Anne Shirley moved to the Four Winds house of dreams, Leslie formed a deep friendship with her, though she initially struggled with feelings of envy over Anne's happy life. When Dr. Gilbert Blythe suggested an operation that might restore the man's memory, Leslie dutifully agreed to take him to a Montreal hospital. The operation proved that the man was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died years earlier of yellow fever in Cuba. Realizing she was free, Leslie eventually confessed her love for writer Owen Ford, who had boarded with her that summer. The two became engaged and were later married, intending to spend their summers at Echo Lodge in Four Winds.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c11 P16](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0016), [v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020), [v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028), [v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011), [v4 c29 P12](../source/v04-c29.md#nw-v04-c29-p0012), [v4 c31 P27](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0027), [v4 c33 P9](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0009), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott of Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- Traumatized in childhood by seeing her younger brother Kenneth killed in an accident  <sub>[v4 c11 P16](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0016)</sub>
- Discovered her father after he committed suicide when she was fourteen  <sub>[v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020)</sub>
- Attended Queen's Academy and taught at the Glen St. Mary school  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022)</sub>
- Forced at age sixteen into marrying Dick Moore to save her mother's home from mortgage foreclosure  <sub>[v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027)</sub>
- Cared for twelve years for an injured, amnesiac man she believed to be her husband Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035)</sub>

## Quotes

> I had a house of dreams once—but it was a palace.  <sub>[v4 c10 P27](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0027)</sub>

> If we are to be friends you must call me Leslie.  <sub>[v4 c10 P29](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0029)</sub>

> I ENVY Anne, and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!  <sub>[v4 c19 P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028)</sub>

> I—I have been a hateful beast, Anne. I hated you because I ENVIED you.  <sub>[v4 c21 P5](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0005)</sub>

> Love triumphant.  <sub>[v4 c38 P8](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0008)</sub>
